args: This is an observation-producing free-air approach, not a grasp. Check the proposed straight pad-center transfer and yaw adjustment to hover_target using the supplied own finger envelope. Is the relevant swept route visibly free of the bowl, bottle, stove and cabinet with at least 10 mm separation? Do not certify occluded clearance. Confirm the registered top patch is still the same cream cheese and no scene displacement is apparent. The contact-height calculation now uses the finite pad face, retaining 6 mm finger/table clearance; side contact will be measured from the closer view before descent.

geometry.assumptions: Observed flat package and horizontal tabletop; full own pad extents give a common contact-height band. Allowance is an engineering reserve, not calibrated confidence. No unseen package bottom or obstacle clearance is asserted.

audit.previous_error: Requiring the pad CENTER below the package top ignored the finite 16 mm pad height.
audit.motion_before_revision: None: same frame and native-step count confirmed.

result.explanation: For the proposed straight free-air transfer and small yaw adjustment only, the visible obstacle geometry supports at least 10 mm separation from the supplied finger envelope. The route passes above the bowl and stove, clears the bottle, and stays laterally away from the cabinet and its handles. Initial hand occlusion is robot self-occlusion, not an observed external obstruction. No hidden-surface clearance or later descent is certified. The registered patch lies on the labeled cream-cheese top. No displacement is apparent in the frame-0 views, with no intervening execution reported. The visible flat top and tabletop support the local finite-pad model assumptions; side contact and final table clearance still require the closer-view check.
